messages:
tanya: Noticed something odd in the Go SDK generator: context cancel seems to only abort the initial request, not an in-flight stream. Repro below.
tanya: snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
stream, _ := client.Generator("redwood/fast-gen").Stream(ctx, req)
// read one token then cancel
first, _ := stream.Recv()
fmt.Println(first.Text)
cancel()
// expecting Recv() to return quickly with error, but it blocks until model finishes
_, err := stream.Recv()
if err != nil { fmt.Println("stopped:", err) }
```
ryan: which transport? http long-poll, SSE, or websocket?
ryan: If the underlying net.Conn isn't closed on ctx.Done(), Recv will hang on Read.
ish: That's a known parity miss vs Python where we close sse/ws on cancel. Should be small to fix.
lee: We intentionally kept the stream read loop separate to avoid mid-stream races, but we didn't add a proper abort API. We should either watch ctx in the read loop or expose Abort().
tanya: Exposing Abort() would be nicer for clarity; otherwise users have to cancel ctx and hope internals handle it.
ish: Agreed. Also add a sample in /samples/go showing Cancel pattern for generators; a lot of folks copy/paste the basic loop.
anya: (typo: tanya)
bot-deploy: [CI] job generator-stream-unit-tests #120 failed: goroutine leak detected
ryan: Action: I'll prototype a minimal change that spawns a goroutine selecting on ctx.Done() to close the transport connection and add tests for no goroutine leaks. If that works, we can follow up with explicit Abort method design.
lee: Good. Make sure Close is idempotent and safe when concurrent Recv is blocked.
ish: I'll add a parity e2e so Python and Go behave the same under client cancel.
tanya: thanks — this was blocking a small demo for me. happy to test once you have a PR. :rocket:
